Subject: SLA template — availability anchor and monthly credits

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to start a short thread to lock down the availability anchor and how monthly crediting would work if we hit exceptions. We have a couple of non-negotiables from our side: a measurable monthly uptime target and a predictable cap on monthly credits so finance can forecast.

Can you send your standard template with a simple example schedule (percent thresholds -> monthly credit %) and an example calculation for a partial-month incident? Also please flag maintenance carveouts and whether latency incidents are treated separately.

If you can loop in whoever owns SLA s and credits on your side that would be great — our procurement lead is on cc.

Thanks,
Sven

Subject: Re: SLA template — availability anchor and monthly credits

Hi Sven — thanks, and great questions.

Attached is SLA_Template_v3.docx and a tiny sample CSV that shows how we'd compute credits in a month with one partial-day incident. High level answers up front:

- Anchor (monthly uptime): 99.95% standard for Hosted API.
- Monthly crediting (example tiers):
  * >= 99.95% — no credit
  * 99.5% to <99.95% — 10% monthly service credit
  * 99.0% to <99.5% — 30% monthly service credit
  * <99.0% — 60% monthly service credit
- Credit cap: we propose a 60% cap of the monthly invoice for availability incidents. That keeps exposure predictable for both sides.
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance (48+ hours notice for major upgrades, <= 4 hours notice for rolling patches) is excluded; emergency maintenance will be documented and is eligible for differentiated treatment per the template.
- Latency: we treat latency SLOs separately from availability; there is an optional latency ladder in the template if you want per-p95 tiers (we can include that in the Doc).

A couple of clarifying Qs for you so we align the doc to your process:
1) Do you want credits applied as dollar offsets on the next invoice, or as service-days (or account-level credits)? We typically apply invoice offsets, but we can add an escrow-style mechanism if your procurement requires it.
2) For partial-month incidents, do you prefer pro-rata calculation by affected seconds (what our sample shows) or the simple per-day bucket approach? The pro-rata gives more granular fairness, the bucket approach is easier operationally.

Internal note: looping in Laura for procurement/legal redline expectations and Hannah for how the maintenance carveout language should read for batched inference workloads.

Ben

- Consider tightening the top tier: 99.98% for customers on annual committed plans (we can keep 99.95% for standard hosted).
- For partial-month incidents, use pro-rata by seconds in the sample CSV but include the simpler per-day example in the doc appendix for legal.

Sven — thanks for the quick review. Ben here with an updated proposal attached. Key changes from the first draft:

- Hosted anchor: 99.95% standard; 99.98% available as a committed-plan option (call out if you want that added to the quote).
- Monthly credit tiers (final proposal):
  * >= 99.95% — 0% credit
  * 99.8% to <99.95% — 10% credit
  * 99.5% to <99.8% — 30% credit
  * <99.5% — 60% credit (cap at 60% of monthly invoice)
- Partial-month calculation: pro-rata by affected seconds (see uptime-metrics-sample.csv for worked example). We included a short per-day example in the appendix of SLA_Template_v3.docx for convenience.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance with >= 4 hours' notice is excluded; emergency maintenance is eligible for differentiated consideration per section 4.2. Regional escalation map included.
- Latency: optional latency ladder included as Appendix B; we can activate it if you want p95 commitments tied to crediting.

Next steps: if procurement confirms invoice-offsets are acceptable (we think this is easiest), we can:
1) Mark up the attached SLA template with any specific language you require (insurance, audit, export controls).
2) Legal will do a fast redline loop (Laura) once we get your preferred credit mechanism.
3) I can send a DocuSign link for signature after redlines. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/ACME-98765
